asr_text: This news feels like a short play in three acts. Act 1 was 20%. Act 2 brought an unexpected turn. Act 3 was an unexpected move in oil prices. The curtain rose on July 13th. At 10:16 a.m., Trump posted that the United States would seek a 20% charge on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The aim was to recover the cost of U.S. efforts to keep the strait safe. But 20% was not a finished system. The post did not say who would pay, how the money would be collected, or what legal basis would support it. For the moment, only a large number stood at center stage. The number stayed at center stage for about a day. Then the story took a sharp turn.
